All ego-browser helpers are preloaded into that script.\\n33:\\n34:## Common helpers\\n35:\\n36:- Task spaces: `listTaskSpaces`, `useOrCreateTaskSpace`, `claimTaskSpace`, `handOffTaskSpace`, `takeOverTaskSpace`, `waitForAgentControl`, `completeTaskSpace`\\n37:- Navigation / state: `listTabs`, `openOrReuseTab`, `closeTab`, `gotoAndWait`, `currentTab`, `switchTab`, `gotoUrl`, `pageInfo`, `ensureRealTab`\\n38:- Observation: `snapshotText`, `captureScreenshot`, `drainEvents`\\n39:- Scroll / mouse: `scrollBy`, `scrollToBottomUntil`, `scroll`, `click`, `doubleClick`, `hover`, `dragMouse`\\n40:- Keyboard & input: `typeText`, `fillInput`, `pressKey`, `dispatchKey`\\n41:- File: `uploadFile`\\n42:- Wait: `wait`, `waitForLoad`, `waitForElement`, `waitForNetworkIdle`\\n43:- Fetch: `serverFetch`, `browserFetch`\\n44:- CDP / evaluate: `js`, `cdp`\\n45:- Output: `cliLog`, `help`\\n46:\\n47:Notes:\\n48:- `cliLog(value)` — prints to the terminal; it is the only output mechanism inside a heredoc, and all final results must go through it.\\n49:- `await pageInfo()` — normally resolves to `{ url, title, w, h, sx, sy, pw, ph }`; if a native browser dialog is open, resolves to `{ dialog: ... }` instead because page JavaScript is blocked.\\n50:- If `await pageInfo()` resolves to `{ dialog: ... }`, handle the dialog with `await cdp('Page.handleJavaScriptDialog', { accept: true })` or `accept: false` before running page JavaScript.\\n51:- `await ensureRealTab()` — switches to an existing non-internal page tab if needed and resolves to it; resolves to `null` when none exists. It does not create a tab — use `await openOrReuseTab(...)` for that.\\n52:- `await closeTab(target?)` — closes the given target id / tab object, or the current tab when omitted.\\n53:- `await drainEvents()` — consumes and returns the async event queue produced by the page (navigation events, network events, etc.).\\n54:- `await serverFetch(url, options)` — issues a request from Node and returns the response body.\\n55:- `await browserFetch(url, options)` — issues a request from the current browser page context and returns the response body.\\n56:- `help(name)` — prints usage for a given helper, e.g. `cliLog(help('click'))`.\\n57:\\n58:\\n59:### Task spaces\\n60:\\n61:A task space is an **isolated browsing context** that ego-browser provides for AI Agents. Each task space has its own set of tabs but **inherits the current user's login state** by default, so Agents can operate on authenticated sites without competing with or disturbing the user's normal browser windows.\\n62:\\n63:Closing all tabs in a task space is equivalent to closing that task space.\\n64:\\n65:A task often takes multiple heredoc rounds to complete. Because the Node.js runtime exits after each heredoc and retains no state, normal working heredocs should start with an explicit call to `useOrCreateTaskSpace(nameOrId)` to reuse the same space — this lets you operate continuously and reuse tabs across rounds. The exception is resuming after a handoff: once the user confirms \\\"continue\\\" (through an Ask or in chat), start the next heredoc with `takeOverTaskSpace(nameOrId)` instead.\\n66:\\n67:`nameOrId` can be a task space name, numeric id, or digit-only numeric id string. String values match `name`/`taskId` first, then digit-only strings fall back to numeric id. Number values match existing numeric ids only; if no matching id exists, `useOrCreateTaskSpace` fails instead of creating a new space.\\n68:\\n69:Use a short name for the active user goal when creating a new task space. Keep reusing that task space for follow-up questions, corrections, refinements, re-checks, and result validation, even if you previously thought the task was complete. Choose a new task space only when the user clearly starts a separate, unrelated goal. Prefer using the numeric `id` returned by `useOrCreateTaskSpace` (for example, `task.id`) to resume a known task in later rounds and avoid name collisions.\\n70:\\n71:For any follow-up on the same user goal — including continue, corrections, retries, validation, user-reported problems, or work after `completeTaskSpace(..., { keep: true })` — resume the original task space first if it still exists. Do not create a new task space for the same goal unless the user asks for a fresh space, starts an unrelated goal, or the original space is unavailable after checking. If a new space is necessary, state why.\\n72:\\n73:After explicit user confirmation, to continue work from an existing user-owned, inactive, or unassigned task space, use `await listTaskSpaces()` to find the space, call `await claimTaskSpace(id)` to take ownership and select it, then use `await listTabs()` and `await switchTab(targetId)` to select the exact tab before acting.\\n74:\\n75:**Ownership policy** — every task space has `ownership: 'agent' | 'agentDelegatedToUser' | 'user'`; the helpers treat user-owned spaces differently:\\n76:\\n77:| Helper | When the target space is user-owned |\\n78:|---|---|\\n79:| `switchTaskSpace` | throws — agent-owned spaces only |\\n80:| `claimTaskSpace` | claims it (ownership transfers to the agent), then selects it |\\n81:| `handOffTaskSpace` | skipped — resolves `{ done: false, skipped: 'user-owned' }` |\\n82:| `completeTaskSpace(…, { keep: true })` | skipped — resolves `{ done: false, skipped: 'user-owned' }` |\\n83:| `completeTaskSpace(…, { keep: false })` | claims it, then closes it |\\n84:| `takeOverTaskSpace` / `waitForAgentControl` | no ownership check |\\n85:\\n86:`handOffTaskSpace` and `completeTaskSpace` resolve `{ done: true }` when the operation actually happened. Check `done` before telling the user the handoff/cleanup is finished — a `skipped` result usually means you targeted a space that was never yours.\\n87:\\n88:**`completeTaskSpace(nameOrId, { keep })` must occupy its own dedicated final heredoc, and run only after a prior heredoc's output has confirmed the task is genuinely done.** `keep` is required and defaults by policy to `false`: close the task space after completion unless there is a concrete reason to leave the live page visible.\\n89:\\n90:Use `{ keep: true }` only when the user explicitly asks to keep the page open, the task needs manual user action in that exact page, or the result cannot be delivered well as a URL, file, artifact, or summary. Do not keep a task space open merely because a page was visited, a document was created, or a screenshot was used for verification.\\n91:\\n92:When passing a string that may create a new task space, the string should reflect the task's intent (e.g. `'search github issues'`); don't use literal placeholders.\\n93:\\n94:**If the task space needs to be preserved after the task ends, keep only the tabs that need to be shown to the user.** Keep loose awareness of how many tabs are open — a quick `(await listTabs()).length` is enough; there's no need to spend a dedicated round just to check. When scratch tabs (search-result pages, cross-check pages, and other one-off pages) pile up, close them as you go rather than letting them all accumulate for the end. When finishing with `{ keep: true }` to leave pages for the user, clear out the remaining scratch tabs so only the pages worth showing stay open. Close a single tab with `await closeTab(targetId)` (`targetId` comes from `listTabs()` or an `openOrReuseTab` return value).\\n95:\\n96:\\n97:### Control handoff\\n98:\\n99:Only one side — agent or user — holds control of a task space at any time. While the user holds control, any browser operation by the agent fails with a \\\"user is controlling\\\" message — do not retry it; follow the steps below to resume.\\n100:\\n101:A \\\"user is controlling\\\" error is a hard stop on the whole task — not an obstacle to route around. It means the user has deliberately taken the browser back, often because your current approach is going wrong. Honoring it *is* the correct outcome here; pushing the goal forward anyway is the failure. The only thing you may do is **ask the user and wait**.\\n102:\\n103:An \\\"inactive\\\", \\\"not assigned to an agent\\\", or similar task-space error is also a hard stop with the same confirmation requirement. Resume only after explicit user confirmation, then start with `await claimTaskSpace(id)`.\\n104:\\n105:**Handing off**: When the task requires user intervention (e.g. login, captcha, manual confirmation), call `await handOffTaskSpace([nameOrId])` to give control to the user, and tell them exactly what to do. Omitting `nameOrId` uses the currently selected task space; pass `task.id` across heredoc rounds to avoid ambiguity.\\n106:\\n107:**Regaining control**: Take control back *only* after the user explicitly confirms — through an Ask (your harness's button/option prompt, e.g. \\\"Continue\\\" vs \\\"Finish task\\\") or a \\\"continue\\\" message in chat. Then start a new heredoc with `await takeOverTaskSpace([nameOrId])` and resume; if the user chooses to finish, close out with `await completeTaskSpace(nameOrId, { keep })`. Never call `takeOverTaskSpace` on your own to grab control back — it has no ownership check and will seize the browser away from the user.\\n108:\\n109:**Unexpected takeover**: The user can take over at any time via the browser GUI — the same effect as the agent calling `handOffTaskSpace`. Do not retry the failed operation and do not auto-takeover; surface the Ask above (Continue / Finish) and resume only when the user picks Continue.\\n110:\\n111:`await waitForAgentControl(nameOrId)` is a read-only blocking poll (it never takes control); use it only to wait inside the current heredoc for a handoff you initiated.\\n112:\\n113:\\n114:### Scroll / mouse\\n115:\\n116:```js\\n117:// DOM scroll\\n118:await scrollBy(900)\\n119:await scrollToBottomUntil(\\n120:  async () => await js(String.raw`document.querySelectorAll('article').length`) >= 20,\\n121:  { step: 900, wait: 1, maxSteps: 20 }\\n122:)\\n123:\\n124:// Real wheel event\\n125:await scroll({ dy: 900 })\\n126:```\\n127:\\n128:Element-target helpers such as `click`, `doubleClick`, `hover`, `dragMouse`, `fillInput`, `uploadFile`, and `waitForElement` accept the same selector/ref surface: raw CSS, `xpath=...`, `@N` / `ref=N`, and `loc=...` values from `snapshotText()` (`loc=css:...`, `loc=role:...`, `loc=href:...`). `@N` refs are for ego-browser helpers only; they are not valid selectors inside `document.querySelector(...)`.\\n129:\\n130:`click`, `doubleClick`, `hover`, and `dragMouse` share these target formats. Coordinates are in CSS pixels:\\n131:\\n132:- `string` — CSS selector, `xpath=...`, `@N` / `ref=N`, or `loc=...`; clicks the element's center.\\n133:- `[x, y]` or `{x, y}` — viewport coordinates.\\n134:- `{selector}` — CSS selector, `xpath=...`, `@N` / `ref=N`, or `loc=...`; clicks the element's center.\\n135:- `{selector, x, y}` — offset from the element's top-left corner by `x`/`y`.\\n136:- `options.label` (optional) — a 3-6 word action description; triggers a visual highlight animation.\\n137:\\n138:```js\\n139:await click('@21', { label: 'check login status' })\\n140:await click('button.primary', { label: 'click submit button' })\\n141:await click([420, 260])\\n142:await click({ x: 420, y: 260 })\\n143:await click({ selector: 'canvas#stage', x: 12, y: 8 })\\n144:await hover('@5', { label: 'hover to reveal menu' })\\n145:await dragMouse([from, to], { label: 'drag card' })\\n146:```\\n147:\\n148:### uploadFile\\n149:\\n150:```js\\n151:await uploadFile('input[type=\\\"file\\\"]', \\\"/absolute/path/to/file.pdf\\\")\\n152:```\\n153:\\n154:### js\\n155:\\n156:`js()` is essentially `Runtime.evaluate` and takes a string. You can pass a function, but doing so triggers a one-time warning and wraps it via `.toString()` — closures are not captured and there is no argument channel. Do not use `js()` the way you would Puppeteer / Playwright's `page.evaluate(fn, ...args)`.\\n157:\\n158:When you need to run multi-step logic inside the browser, wrap it in a single self-invoking closure and return once — don't split it across multiple `await js()` calls:\\n159:\\n160:```js\\n161:const data = await js(String.raw`(() => {\\n162:  const items = [...document.querySelectorAll('article')]\\n163:  return items.map(el => ({\\n164:    text: el.innerText,\\n165:    links: [...el.querySelectorAll('a')].map(a => a.href),\\n166:  }))\\n167:})()`)\\n168:```\\n169:\\n170:\\n171:## Recommended workflow\\n172:\\n173:ego-browser has three main workflows. AI Agents work in their own isolated space, reusing the user's login state without competing for the browser. Use this skill whenever the user needs to interact with a website opening pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting page data, testing web apps, logging into sites, automating browser operations, or any other browser automation task. Triggers include requests to \\\"open a website\\\", \\\"visit a URL\\\", \\\"fill out a form\\\", \\\"click a button\\\", \\\"take a screenshot\\\", \\\"scrape data from a page\\\", \\\"extract content from a page\\\", \\\"test this web app\\\", \\\"login to a site\\\", \\\"automate browser actions\\\", or any …\\nmetadata:\\n  version: \\\"1.2.3\\\"\\n  date: \\\"2026-06-25\\\"\\n---\\n\\n# ego-browser\\n\\nego-browser gives AI agents a CLI-accessible Node.js runtime, with built-in helpers — snapshotText, click, js, cdp, and more — that agents call directly inside JS scripts to observe pages, interact with UI, evaluate browser-side JavaScript, and drive a real browser for any web automation task.\\n\\nFor setup, install, or connection problems, read `references/install.md`.\\n\\nUse the `Bash` tool to run all browser operations via `ego-browser nodejs <<'EOF' ... EOF` heredoc. Do not write code to a `.js` file first.\\n\\n\\n## Quick start\\n\\n```bash\\nego-browser nodejs <<'EOF'\\n// Name the task space for the whole user task, then reuse that space across heredoc rounds.\\nconst task = await useOrCreateTaskSpace('inspect example page')\\ncliLog('task space id: ' + task.id)\\n\\nawait openOrReuseTab('https://example.com', { wait: true, timeout: 20 })\\n\\ncliLog(await snapshotText())\\nEOF\\n```\\n\\nThe heredoc body runs as a Node.js script that controls the selected ego-browser task space. All ego-browser helpers are preloaded into that script.\\n\\n## Common helpers\\n\\n- Task spaces: `listTaskSpaces`, `useOrCreateTaskSpace`, `claimTaskSpace`, `handOffTaskSpace`, `takeOverTaskSpace`, `waitForAgentControl`, `completeTaskSpace`\\n- Navigation / state: `listTabs`, `openOrReuseTab`, `closeTab`, `gotoAndWait`, `currentTab`, `switchTab`, `gotoUrl`, `pageInfo`, `ensureRealTab`\\n- Observation: `snapshotText`, `captureScreenshot`, `drainEvents`\\n- Scroll / mouse: `scrollBy`, `scrollToBottomUntil`, `scroll`, `click`, `doubleClick`, `hover`, `dragMouse`\\n- Keyboard & input: `typeText`, `fillInput`, `pressKey`, `dispatchKey`\\n- File: `uploadFile`\\n- Wait: `wait`, `waitForLoad`, `waitForElement`, `waitForNetworkIdle`\\n- Fetch: `serverFetch`, `browserFetch`\\n- CDP / evaluate: `js`, `cdp`\\n- Output: `cliLog`, `help`\\n\\nNotes:\\n- `cliLog(value)` — prints to the terminal; it is the only output mechanism inside a heredoc, and all final results must go through it.\\n- `await pageInfo()` — normally resolves to `{ url, title, w, h, sx, sy, pw, ph }`; if a native browser dialog is open, resolves to `{ dialog: ... }` instead because page JavaScript is blocked.\\n- If `await pageInfo()` resolves to `{ dialog: ... }`, handle the dialog with `await cdp('Page.handleJavaScriptDialog', { accept: true })` or `accept: false` before running page JavaScript.\\n- `await ensureRealTab()` — switches to an existing non-internal page tab if needed and resolves to it; resolves to `null` when none exists. It does not create a tab — use `await openOrReuseTab(...)` for that.\\n- `await closeTab(target?)` — closes the given target id / tab object, or the current tab when omitted.\\n- `await drainEvents()` — consumes and returns the async event queue produced by the page (navigation events, network events, etc.).\\n- `await serverFetch(url, options)` — issues a request from Node and returns the response body.\\n- `await browserFetch(url, options)` — issues a request from the current browser page context and returns the response body.\\n- `help(name)` — prints usage for a given helper, e.g. `cliLog(help('click'))`.\\n\\n\\n### Task spaces\\n\\nA task space is an **isolated browsing context** that ego-browser provides for AI Agents. Each task space has its own set of tabs but **inherits the current user's login state** by default, so Agents can operate on authenticated sites without competing with or disturbing the user's normal browser windows.\\n\\nClosing all tabs in a task space is equivalent to closing that task space.\\n\\nA task often takes multiple heredoc rounds to complete. Because the Node.js runtime exits after each heredoc and retains no state, normal working heredocs should start with an explicit call to `useOrCreateTaskSpace(nameOrId)` to reuse the same space — this lets you operate continuously and reuse tabs across rounds. The exception is resuming after a handoff: once the user confirms \\\"continue\\\" (through an Ask or in chat), start the next heredoc with `takeOverTaskSpace(nameOrId)` instead.\\n\\n`nameOrId` can be a task space name, numeric id, or digit-only numeric id string. String values match `name`/`taskId` first, then digit-only strings fall back to numeric id. Number values match existing numeric ids only; if no matching id exists, `useOrCreateTaskSpace` fails instead of creating a new space.\\n\\nUse a short name for the active user goal when creating a new task space. Keep reusing that task space for follow-up questions, corrections, refinements, re-checks, and result validation, even if you previously thought the task was complete. Choose a new task space only when the user clearly starts a separate, unrelated goal. Prefer using the numeric `id` returned by `useOrCreateTaskSpace` (for example, `task.id`) to resume a known task in later rounds and avoid name collisions.\\n\\nFor any follow-up on the same user goal — including continue, corrections, retries, validation, user-reported problems, or work after `completeTaskSpace(..., { keep: true })` — resume the original task space first if it still exists. Do not create a new task space for the same goal unless the user asks for a fresh space, starts an unrelated goal, or the original space is unavailable after checking. If a new space is necessary, state why.\\n\\nAfter explicit user confirmation, to continue work from an existing user-owned, inactive, or unassigned task space, use `await listTaskSpaces()` to find the space, call `await claimTaskSpace(id)` to take ownership and select it, then use `await listTabs()` and `await switchTab(targetId)` to select the exact tab before acting.\\n\\n**Ownership policy** — every task space has `ownership: 'agent' | 'agentDelegatedToUser' | 'user'`; the helpers treat user-owned spaces differently:\\n\\n| Helper | When the target space is user-owned |\\n|---|---|\\n| `switchTaskSpace` | throws — agent-owned spaces only |\\n| `claimTaskSpace` | claims it (ownership transfers to the agent), then selects it |\\n| `handOffTaskSpace` | skipped — resolves `{ done: false, skipped: 'user-owned' }` |\\n| `completeTaskSpace(…, { keep: true })` | skipped — resolves `{ done: false, skipped: 'user-owned' }` |\\n| `completeTaskSpace(…, { keep: false })` | claims it, then closes it |\\n| `takeOverTaskSpace` / `waitForAgentControl` | no ownership check |\\n\\n`handOffTaskSpace` and `completeTaskSpace` resolve `{ done: true }` when the operation actually happened. Check `done` before telling the user the handoff/cleanup is finished — a `skipped` result usually means you targeted a space that was never yours.\\n\\n**`completeTaskSpace(nameOrId, { keep })` must occupy its own dedicated final heredoc, and run only after a prior heredoc's output has confirmed the task is genuinely done.** `keep` is required and defaults by policy to `false`: close the task space after completion unless there is a concrete reason to leave the live page visible.\\n\\nUse `{ keep: true }` only when the user explicitly asks to keep the page open, the task needs manual user action in that exact page, or the result cannot be delivered well as a URL, file, artifact, or summary. Do not keep a task space open merely because a page was visited, a document was created, or a screenshot was used for verification.\\n\\nWhen passing a string that may create a new task space, the string should reflect the task's intent (e.g. `'search github issues'`); don't use literal placeholders.\\n\\n**If the task space needs to be preserved after the task ends, keep only the tabs that need to be shown to the user.** Keep loose awareness of how many tabs are open — a quick `(await listTabs()).length` is enough; there's no need to spend a dedicated round just to check. When scratch tabs (search-result pages, cross-check pages, and other one-off pages) pile up, close them as you go rather than letting them all accumulate for the end. When finishing with `{ keep: true }` to leave pages for the user, clear out the remaining scratch tabs so only the pages worth showing stay open. Close a single tab with `await closeTab(targetId)` (`targetId` comes from `listTabs()` or an `openOrReuseTab` return value).\\n\\n\\n### Control handoff\\n\\nOnly one side — agent or user — holds control of a task space at any time. While the user holds control, any browser operation by the agent fails with a \\\"user is controlling\\\" message — do not retry it; follow the steps below to resume.\\n\\nA \\\"user is controlling\\\" error is a hard stop on the whole task — not an obstacle to route around. It means the user has deliberately taken the browser back, often because your current approach is going wrong. Honoring it *is* the correct outcome here; pushing the goal forward anyway is the failure. The only thing you may do is **ask the user and wait**.\\n\\nAn \\\"inactive\\\", \\\"not assigned to an agent\\\", or similar task-space error is also a hard stop with the same confirmation requirement. Resume only after explicit user confirmation, then start with `await claimTaskSpace(id)`.\\n\\n**Handing off**: When the task requires user intervention (e.g. login, captcha, manual confirmation), call `await handOffTaskSpace([nameOrId])` to give control to the user, and tell them exactly what to do. Omitting `nameOrId` uses the currently selected task space; pass `task.id` across heredoc rounds to avoid ambiguity.\\n\\n**Regaining control**: Take control back *only* after the user explicitly confirms — through an Ask (your harness's button/option prompt, e.g. \\\"Continue\\\" vs \\\"Finish task\\\") or a \\\"continue\\\" message in chat. Then start a new heredoc with `await takeOverTaskSpace([nameOrId])` and resume; if the user chooses to finish, close out with `await completeTaskSpace(nameOrId, { keep })`. Never call `takeOverTaskSpace` on your own to grab control back — it has no ownership check and will seize the browser away from the user.\\n\\n**Unexpected takeover**: The user can take over at any time via the browser GUI — the same effect as the agent calling `handOffTaskSpace`. Do not retry the failed operation and do not auto-takeover; surface the Ask above (Continue / Finish) and resume only when the user picks Continue.\\n\\n`await waitForAgentControl(nameOrId)` is a read-only blocking poll (it never takes control); use it only to wait inside the current heredoc for a handoff you initiated.\\n\\n\\n### Scroll / mouse\\n\\n```js\\n// DOM scroll\\nawait scrollBy(900)\\nawait scrollToBottomUntil(\\n  async () => await js(String.raw`document.querySelectorAll('article').length`) >= 20,\\n  { step: 900, wait: 1, maxSteps: 20 }\\n)\\n\\n// Real wheel event\\nawait scroll({ dy: 900 })\\n```\\n\\nElement-target helpers such as `click`, `doubleClick`, `hover`, `dragMouse`, `fillInput`, `uploadFile`, and `waitForElement` accept the same selector/ref surface: raw CSS, `xpath=...`, `@N` / `ref=N`, and `loc=...` values from `snapshotText()` (`loc=css:...`, `loc=role:...`, `loc=href:...`). `@N` refs are for ego-browser helpers only; they are not valid selectors inside `document.querySelector(...)`.\\n\\n`click`, `doubleClick`, `hover`, and `dragMouse` share these target formats. Coordinates are in CSS pixels:\\n\\n- `string` — CSS selector, `xpath=...`, `@N` / `ref=N`, or `loc=...`; clicks the element's center.\\n- `[x, y]` or `{x, y}` — viewport coordinates.\\n- `{selector}` — CSS selector, `xpath=...`, `@N` / `ref=N`, or `loc=...`; clicks the element's center.\\n- `{selector, x, y}` — offset from the element's top-left corner by `x`/`y`.\\n- `options.label` (optional) — a 3-6 word action description; triggers a visual highlight animation.\\n\\n```js\\nawait click('@21', { label: 'check login status' })\\nawait click('button.primary', { label: 'click submit button' })\\nawait click([420, 260])\\nawait click({ x: 420, y: 260 })\\nawait click({ selector: 'canvas#stage', x: 12, y: 8 })\\nawait hover('@5', { label: 'hover to reveal menu' })\\nawait dragMouse([from, to], { label: 'drag card' })\\n```\\n\\n### uploadFile\\n\\n```js\\nawait uploadFile('input[type=\\\"file\\\"]', \\\"/absolute/path/to/file.pdf\\\")\\n```\\n\\n### js\\n\\n`js()` is essentially `Runtime.evaluate` and takes a string. You can pass a function, but doing so triggers a one-time warning and wraps it via `.toString()` — closures are not captured and there is no argument channel. Do not use `js()` the way you would Puppeteer / Playwright's `page.evaluate(fn, ...args)`.\\n\\nWhen you need to run multi-step logic inside the browser, wrap it in a single self-invoking closure and return once — don't split it across multiple `await js()` calls:\\n\\n```js\\nconst data = await js(String.raw`(() => {\\n  const items = [...document.querySelectorAll('article')]\\n  return items.map(el => ({\\n    text: el.innerText,\\n    links: [...el.querySelectorAll('a')].map(a => a.href),\\n  }))\\n})()`)\\n```\\n\\n\\n## Recommended workflow\\n\\nego-browser has three main workflows. Pick the workflow that fits the page and task before acting.\\n\\nUse the semantic workflow first for ordinary websites with real DOM controls. For canvas-like productivity apps and rich editors — including Google Docs, Google Sheets, Lark/Feishu Docs, Notion, Figma, whiteboards, maps, and other virtualized editors — use the visual workflow first for the main editing surface. These apps often expose toolbars, title inputs, hidden textareas, offscreen iframes, or canvas layers in the DOM that do not represent the actual user-editable document or grid. Do not rely on `await fillInput(...)`, DOM selectors, or `snapshotText()` refs for the main editing surface unless a small write probe proves the text lands in the intended place.\\n\\nBefore writing substantial content into a rich editor, perform a tiny write probe, then verify it with `await captureScreenshot()`, an export/readback path, or another reliable visual/state check. If the probe appears in the title bar, toolbar search, hidden input, or any wrong field, stop using DOM/input helpers for that surface and switch to screenshot-guided mouse actions plus real keyboard operations.\\n\\n1. **Semantic workflow: `snapshotText()` + refs / locators** — default for most pages with normal text, links, buttons, forms, tables, and lists.\\n   - Reuse or create a task space: `const task = await useOrCreateTaskSpace(name)`.\\n   - Open or switch pages with `await openOrReuseTab(url, { wait: true })`; use `await gotoAndWait(url, { timeout, settle })` only when navigating inside the current tab.\\n   - Observe with `await snapshotText()` to get a full-page semantic tree annotated with `[ref=N, loc=..., url=...]`.\\n   - Act with `await click('@N')`, `await fillInput('@N', ...)`, or stable `loc=...` values. Use direct DOM logic only when it is simpler than helper calls.\\n   - After meaningful clicks, input, or navigation, observe again with `await snapshotText()`, `await pageInfo()`, or `await captureScreenshot()` before assuming success.\\n\\n2. **Visual workflow: `await captureScreenshot()` + coordinate/keyboard actions** — use when the page is primarily visual, canvas-like, heavily virtualized, or when accessibility / semantic structure is incomplete.\\n   - Inspect the screenshot, act with viewport coordinates such as `await click([x, y])`, `await doubleClick([x, y])`, `await pressKey(...)`, and `await typeText(...)`, then verify with another screenshot or a reliable export/readback path.\\n   - Prefer this path for rich editors, spreadsheets, visual menus, map/canvas UIs, drag interactions, and targets that are obvious visually but poor in the DOM/AX tree.\\n\\n3. **Direct DOM / CDP workflow: `await js(...)` / `await cdp(...)`** — use when you need browser state, compact data extraction, custom DOM traversal, or raw browser capabilities.\\n   - Keep browser-side logic in one explicit IIFE and return once.\\n   - Use `await cdp(...)` for browser protocol operations that helpers do not cover.\\n\\nThese workflows can be combined. A task may take multiple heredoc rounds when the next step depends on fresh page state or user handoff. In each round, write a coherent script that advances the task: observe, act or extract, verify, and report with `cliLog(...)`. Avoid tiny probe scripts, but don't force the whole task into one oversized script.\\n\\n\\n## Caveats\\n\\n- `wait(...)` and `timeout` values are in **seconds**; only parameters whose names end in `Ms` are milliseconds.\\n- `snapshotText()` defaults to `scope: 'full_page'`, covering the whole page. Use the default in almost every case; only pass `scope: 'only_within_viewport'` when the task needs only visible content.\\n- `@N` refs are only valid for the most recent `snapshotText` call — every call rebuilds the refMap. Ref numbers come from the CDP `backendNodeId`, so the same element keeps the same number across calls; but to use `@N`, N must appear in the latest snapshotText output. An element scrolled out of the viewport, a DOM re-render, or a previous call with `scope:'only_within_viewport'` that didn't cover the element will all cause `Unknown ref`. For elements you need to reference long-term, use the `loc=...` value from snapshotText output as a stable selector, or write a CSS selector directly.\\n- `js()` returns the evaluated result, not a JSON string — don't wrap it with `JSON.parse(...)`.\\n- Inside a `js(...)` template string, regex backslashes must be doubled (e.g. `\\\\\\\\d`, `\\\\\\\\s`), or use `String.raw`.\\n- If the source passed to `js()` contains a top-level `return`, it will be auto-wrapped in an IIFE; `return` inside nested callbacks can also trigger this accidentally. For complex expressions, prefer the explicit `(() => { ... })()` form.\\n- If `await pageInfo()` reports `w: 0` or `h: 0`, do not continue coordinate actions or screenshots until the viewport is fixed. AI Agents work in their own isolated space, reusing the user's login state without competing for the browser. Use this skill whenever the user needs to interact with a website opening pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting page data, testing web apps, logging into sites, automating browser operations, or any other browser automation task. Triggers include requests to \\\"open a website\\\", \\\"visit a URL\\\", \\\"fill out a form\\\", \\\"click a button\\\", \\\"take a screenshot\\\", \\\"scrape data from a page\\\", \\\"extract content from a page\\\", \\\"test this web app\\\", \\\"login to a site\\\", \\\"automate browser actions\\\", or any …\\n4:metadata:\\n5:  version: \\\"1.2.3\\\"\\n6:  date: \\\"2026-06-25\\\"\\n7:---\\n8:\\n9:# ego-browser\\n10:\\n11:ego-browser gives AI agents a CLI-accessible Node.js runtime, with built-in helpers — snapshotText, click, js, cdp, and more — that agents call directly inside JS scripts to observe pages, interact with UI, evaluate browser-side JavaScript, and drive a real browser for any web automation task.\\n12:\\n13:For setup, install, or connection problems, read `references/install.md`.\\n14:\\n15:Use the `Bash` tool to run all browser operations via `ego-browser nodejs <<'EOF' ... EOF` heredoc. Do not write code to a `.js` file first.\\n16:\\n17:\\n18:## Quick start\\n19:\\n20:```bash\\n21:ego-browser nodejs <<'EOF'\\n22:// Name the task space for the whole user task, then reuse that space across heredoc rounds.\\n23:const task = await useOrCreateTaskSpace('inspect example page')\\n24:cliLog('task space id: ' + task.id)\\n25:\\n26:await openOrReuseTab('https://example.com', { wait: true, timeout: 20 })\\n27:\\n28:cliLog(await snapshotText())\\n29:EOF\\n30:```\\n31:\\n32:The heredoc body runs as a Node.js script that controls the selected ego-browser task space. All ego-browser helpers are preloaded into that script.\\n33:\\n34:## Common helpers\\n35:\\n36:- Task spaces: `listTaskSpaces`, `useOrCreateTaskSpace`, `claimTaskSpace`, `handOffTaskSpace`, `takeOverTaskSpace`, `waitForAgentControl`, `completeTaskSpace`\\n37:- Navigation / state: `listTabs`, `openOrReuseTab`, `closeTab`, `gotoAndWait`, `currentTab`, `switchTab`, `gotoUrl`, `pageInfo`, `ensureRealTab`\\n38:- Observation: `snapshotText`, `captureScreenshot`, `drainEvents`\\n39:- Scroll / mouse: `scrollBy`, `scrollToBottomUntil`, `scroll`, `click`, `doubleClick`, `hover`, `dragMouse`\\n40:- Keyboard & input: `typeText`, `fillInput`, `pressKey`, `dispatchKey`\\n41:- File: `uploadFile`\\n42:- Wait: `wait`, `waitForLoad`, `waitForElement`, `waitForNetworkIdle`\\n43:- Fetch: `serverFetch`, `browserFetch`\\n44:- CDP / evaluate: `js`, `cdp`\\n45:- Output: `cliLog`, `help`\\n46:\\n47:Notes:\\n48:- `cliLog(value)` — prints to the terminal; it is the only output mechanism inside a heredoc, and all final results must go through it.\\n49:- `await pageInfo()` — normally resolves to `{ url, title, w, h, sx, sy, pw, ph }`; if a native browser dialog is open, resolves to `{ dialog: ... }` instead because page JavaScript is blocked.\\n50:- If `await pageInfo()` resolves to `{ dialog: ... }`, handle the dialog with `await cdp('Page.handleJavaScriptDialog', { accept: true })` or `accept: false` before running page JavaScript.\\n51:- `await ensureRealTab()` — switches to an existing non-internal page tab if needed and resolves to it; resolves to `null` when none exists. It does not create a tab — use `await openOrReuseTab(...)` for that.\\n52:- `await closeTab(target?)` — closes the given target id / tab object, or the current tab when omitted.\\n53:- `await drainEvents()` — consumes and returns the async event queue produced by the page (navigation events, network events, etc.).\\n54:- `await serverFetch(url, options)` — issues a request from Node and returns the response body.\\n55:- `await browserFetch(url, options)` — issues a request from the current browser page context and returns the response body.\\n56:- `help(name)` — prints usage for a given helper, e.g. `cliLog(help('click'))`.\\n57:\\n58:\\n59:### Task spaces\\n60:\\n61:A task space is an **isolated browsing context** that ego-browser provides for AI Agents. Each task space has its own set of tabs but **inherits the current user's login state** by default, so Agents can operate on authenticated sites without competing with or disturbing the user's normal browser windows.\\n62:\\n63:Closing all tabs in a task space is equivalent to closing that task space.\\n64:\\n65:A task often takes multiple heredoc rounds to complete. Because the Node.js runtime exits after each heredoc and retains no state, normal working heredocs should start with an explicit call to `useOrCreateTaskSpace(nameOrId)` to reuse the same space — this lets you operate continuously and reuse tabs across rounds. The exception is resuming after a handoff: once the user confirms \\\"continue\\\" (through an Ask or in chat), start the next heredoc with `takeOverTaskSpace(nameOrId)` instead.\\n66:\\n67:`nameOrId` can be a task space name, numeric id, or digit-only numeric id string. String values match `name`/`taskId` first, then digit-only strings fall back to numeric id. Number values match existing numeric ids only; if no matching id exists, `useOrCreateTaskSpace` fails instead of creating a new space.\\n68:\\n69:Use a short name for the active user goal when creating a new task space. Keep reusing that task space for follow-up questions, corrections, refinements, re-checks, and result validation, even if you previously thought the task was complete. Choose a new task space only when the user clearly starts a separate, unrelated goal. Prefer using the numeric `id` returned by `useOrCreateTaskSpace` (for example, `task.id`) to resume a known task in later rounds and avoid name collisions.\\n70:\\n71:For any follow-up on the same user goal — including continue, corrections, retries, validation, user-reported problems, or work after `completeTaskSpace(..., { keep: true })` — resume the original task space first if it still exists. Do not create a new task space for the same goal unless the user asks for a fresh space, starts an unrelated goal, or the original space is unavailable after checking. If a new space is necessary, state why.\\n72:\\n73:After explicit user confirmation, to continue work from an existing user-owned, inactive, or unassigned task space, use `await listTaskSpaces()` to find the space, call `await claimTaskSpace(id)` to take ownership and select it, then use `await listTabs()` and `await switchTab(targetId)` to select the exact tab before acting.\\n74:\\n75:**Ownership policy** — every task space has `ownership: 'agent' | 'agentDelegatedToUser' | 'user'`; the helpers treat user-owned spaces differently:\\n76:\\n77:| Helper | When the target space is user-owned |\\n78:|---|---|\\n79:| `switchTaskSpace` | throws — agent-owned spaces only |\\n80:| `claimTaskSpace` | claims it (ownership transfers to the agent), then selects it |\\n81:| `handOffTaskSpace` | skipped — resolves `{ done: false, skipped: 'user-owned' }` |\\n82:| `completeTaskSpace(…, { keep: true })` | skipped — resolves `{ done: false, skipped: 'user-owned' }` |\\n83:| `completeTaskSpace(…, { keep: false })` | claims it, then closes it |\\n84:| `takeOverTaskSpace` / `waitForAgentControl` | no ownership check |\\n85:\\n86:`handOffTaskSpace` and `completeTaskSpace` resolve `{ done: true }` when the operation actually happened. Check `done` before telling the user the handoff/cleanup is finished — a `skipped` result usually means you targeted a space that was never yours.\\n87:\\n88:**`completeTaskSpace(nameOrId, { keep })` must occupy its own dedicated final heredoc, and run only after a prior heredoc's output has confirmed the task is genuinely done.** `keep` is required and defaults by policy to `false`: close the task space after completion unless there is a concrete reason to leave the live page visible.\\n89:\\n90:Use `{ keep: true }` only when the user explicitly asks to keep the page open, the task needs manual user action in that exact page, or the result cannot be delivered well as a URL, file, artifact, or summary. Do not keep a task space open merely because a page was visited, a document was created, or a screenshot was used for verification.\\n91:\\n92:When passing a string that may create a new task space, the string should reflect the task's intent (e.g. `'search github issues'`); don't use literal placeholders.\\n93:\\n94:**If the task space needs to be preserved after the task ends, keep only the tabs that need to be shown to the user.** Keep loose awareness of how many tabs are open — a quick `(await listTabs()).length` is enough; there's no need to spend a dedicated round just to check. When scratch tabs (search-result pages, cross-check pages, and other one-off pages) pile up, close them as you go rather than letting them all accumulate for the end. When finishing with `{ keep: true }` to leave pages for the user, clear out the remaining scratch tabs so only the pages worth showing stay open. Close a single tab with `await closeTab(targetId)` (`targetId` comes from `listTabs()` or an `openOrReuseTab` return value).\\n95:\\n96:\\n97:### Control handoff\\n98:\\n99:Only one side — agent or user — holds control of a task space at any time. While the user holds control, any browser operation by the agent fails with a \\\"user is controlling\\\" message — do not retry it; follow the steps below to resume.\\n100:\\n101:A \\\"user is controlling\\\" error is a hard stop on the whole task — not an obstacle to route around. It means the user has deliberately taken the browser back, often because your current approach is going wrong. Honoring it *is* the correct outcome here; pushing the goal forward anyway is the failure. The only thing you may do is **ask the user and wait**.\\n102:\\n103:An \\\"inactive\\\", \\\"not assigned to an agent\\\", or similar task-space error is also a hard stop with the same confirmation requirement. Resume only after explicit user confirmation, then start with `await claimTaskSpace(id)`.\\n104:\\n105:**Handing off**: When the task requires user intervention (e.g. login, captcha, manual confirmation), call `await handOffTaskSpace([nameOrId])` to give control to the user, and tell them exactly what to do. Omitting `nameOrId` uses the currently selected task space; pass `task.id` across heredoc rounds to avoid ambiguity.\\n106:\\n107:**Regaining control**: Take control back *only* after the user explicitly confirms — through an Ask (your harness's button/option prompt, e.g. \\\"Continue\\\" vs \\\"Finish task\\\") or a \\\"continue\\\" message in chat. Then start a new heredoc with `await takeOverTaskSpace([nameOrId])` and resume; if the user chooses to finish, close out with `await completeTaskSpace(nameOrId, { keep })`. Never call `takeOverTaskSpace` on your own to grab control back — it has no ownership check and will seize the browser away from the user.\\n108:\\n109:**Unexpected takeover**: The user can take over at any time via the browser GUI — the same effect as the agent calling `handOffTaskSpace`. Do not retry the failed operation and do not auto-takeover; surface the Ask above (Continue / Finish) and resume only when the user picks Continue.\\n110:\\n111:`await waitForAgentControl(nameOrId)` is a read-only blocking poll (it never takes control); use it only to wait inside the current heredoc for a handoff you initiated.\\n112:\\n113:\\n114:### Scroll / mouse\\n115:\\n116:```js\\n117:// DOM scroll\\n118:await scrollBy(900)\\n119:await scrollToBottomUntil(\\n120:  async () => await js(String.raw`document.querySelectorAll('article').length`) >= 20,\\n121:  { step: 900, wait: 1, maxSteps: 20 }\\n122:)\\n123:\\n124:// Real wheel event\\n125:await scroll({ dy: 900 })\\n126:```\\n127:\\n128:Element-target helpers such as `click`, `doubleClick`, `hover`, `dragMouse`, `fillInput`, `uploadFile`, and `waitForElement` accept the same selector/ref surface: raw CSS, `xpath=...`, `@N` / `ref=N`, and `loc=...` values from `snapshotText()` (`loc=css:...`, `loc=role:...`, `loc=href:...`). `@N` refs are for ego-browser helpers only; they are not valid selectors inside `document.querySelector(...)`.\\n129:\\n130:`click`, `doubleClick`, `hover`, and `dragMouse` share these target formats. Coordinates are in CSS pixels:\\n131:\\n132:- `string` — CSS selector, `xpath=...`, `@N` / `ref=N`, or `loc=...`; clicks the element's center.\\n133:- `[x, y]` or `{x, y}` — viewport coordinates.\\n134:- `{selector}` — CSS selector, `xpath=...`, `@N` / `ref=N`, or `loc=...`; clicks the element's center.\\n135:- `{selector, x, y}` — offset from the element's top-left corner by `x`/`y`.\\n136:- `options.label` (optional) — a 3-6 word action description; triggers a visual highlight animation.\\n137:\\n138:```js\\n139:await click('@21', { label: 'check login status' })\\n140:await click('button.primary', { label: 'click submit button' })\\n141:await click([420, 260])\\n142:await click({ x: 420, y: 260 })\\n143:await click({ selector: 'canvas#stage', x: 12, y: 8 })\\n144:await hover('@5', { label: 'hover to reveal menu' })\\n145:await dragMouse([from, to], { label: 'drag card' })\\n146:```\\n147:\\n148:### uploadFile\\n149:\\n150:```js\\n151:await uploadFile('input[type=\\\"file\\\"]', \\\"/absolute/path/to/file.pdf\\\")\\n152:```\\n153:\\n154:### js\\n155:\\n156:`js()` is essentially `Runtime.evaluate` and takes a string. You can pass a function, but doing so triggers a one-time warning and wraps it via `.toString()` — closures are not captured and there is no argument channel. Do not use `js()` the way you would Puppeteer / Playwright's `page.evaluate(fn, ...args)`.\\n157:\\n158:When you need to run multi-step logic inside the browser, wrap it in a single self-invoking closure and return once — don't split it across multiple `await js()` calls:\\n159:\\n160:```js\\n161:const data = await js(String.raw`(() => {\\n162:  const items = [...document.querySelectorAll('article')]\\n163:  return items.map(el => ({\\n164:    text: el.innerText,\\n165:    links: [...el.querySelectorAll('a')].map(a => a.href),\\n166:  }))\\n167:})()`)\\n168:```\\n169:\\n170:\\n171:## Recommended workflow\\n172:\\n173:ego-browser has three main workflows. Pick the workflow that fits the page and task before acting.\\n174:\\n175:Use the semantic workflow first for ordinary websites with real DOM controls. For canvas-like productivity apps and rich editors — including Google Docs, Google Sheets, Lark/Feishu Docs, Notion, Figma, whiteboards, maps, and other virtualized editors — use the visual workflow first for the main editing surface. AI Agents work in their own isolated space, reusing the user's login state without competing for the browser. Use this skill whenever the user needs to interact with a website opening pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting page data, testing web apps, logging into sites, automating browser operations, or any other browser automation task. Triggers include requests to \\\"open a website\\\", \\\"visit a URL\\\", \\\"fill out a form\\\", \\\"click a button\\\", \\\"take a screenshot\\\", \\\"scrape data from a page\\\", \\\"extract content from a page\\\", \\\"test this web app\\\", \\\"login to a site\\\", \\\"automate browser actions\\\", or any …\\nmetadata:\\n  version: \\\"1.2.3\\\"\\n  date: \\\"2026-06-25\\\"\\n---\\n\\n# ego-browser\\n\\nego-browser gives AI agents a CLI-accessible Node.js runtime, with built-in helpers — snapshotText, click, js, cdp, and more — that agents call directly inside JS scripts to observe pages, interact with UI, evaluate browser-side JavaScript, and drive a real browser for any web automation task.\\n\\nFor setup, install, or connection problems, read `references/install.md`.\\n\\nUse the `Bash` tool to run all browser operations via `ego-browser nodejs <<'EOF' ... EOF` heredoc. Do not write code to a `.js` file first.\\n\\n\\n## Quick start\\n\\n```bash\\nego-browser nodejs <<'EOF'\\n// Name the task space for the whole user task, then reuse that space across heredoc rounds.\\nconst task = await useOrCreateTaskSpace('inspect example page')\\ncliLog('task space id: ' + task.id)\\n\\nawait openOrReuseTab('https://example.com', { wait: true, timeout: 20 })\\n\\ncliLog(await snapshotText())\\nEOF\\n```\\n\\nThe heredoc body runs as a Node.js script that controls the selected ego-browser task space. All ego-browser helpers are preloaded into that script.\\n\\n## Common helpers\\n\\n- Task spaces: `listTaskSpaces`, `useOrCreateTaskSpace`, `claimTaskSpace`, `handOffTaskSpace`, `takeOverTaskSpace`, `waitForAgentControl`, `completeTaskSpace`\\n- Navigation / state: `listTabs`, `openOrReuseTab`, `closeTab`, `gotoAndWait`, `currentTab`, `switchTab`, `gotoUrl`, `pageInfo`, `ensureRealTab`\\n- Observation: `snapshotText`, `captureScreenshot`, `drainEvents`\\n- Scroll / mouse: `scrollBy`, `scrollToBottomUntil`, `scroll`, `click`, `doubleClick`, `hover`, `dragMouse`\\n- Keyboard & input: `typeText`, `fillInput`, `pressKey`, `dispatchKey`\\n- File: `uploadFile`\\n- Wait: `wait`, `waitForLoad`, `waitForElement`, `waitForNetworkIdle`\\n- Fetch: `serverFetch`, `browserFetch`\\n- CDP / evaluate: `js`, `cdp`\\n- Output: `cliLog`, `help`\\n\\nNotes:\\n- `cliLog(value)` — prints to the terminal; it is the only output mechanism inside a heredoc, and all final results must go through it.\\n- `await pageInfo()` — normally resolves to `{ url, title, w, h, sx, sy, pw, ph }`; if a native browser dialog is open, resolves to `{ dialog: ... }` instead because page JavaScript is blocked.\\n- If `await pageInfo()` resolves to `{ dialog: ... }`, handle the dialog with `await cdp('Page.handleJavaScriptDialog', { accept: true })` or `accept: false` before running page JavaScript.\\n- `await ensureRealTab()` — switches to an existing non-internal page tab if needed and resolves to it; resolves to `null` when none exists. It does not create a tab — use `await openOrReuseTab(...)` for that.\\n- `await closeTab(target?)` — closes the given target id / tab object, or the current tab when omitted.\\n- `await drainEvents()` — consumes and returns the async event queue produced by the page (navigation events, network events, etc.).\\n- `await serverFetch(url, options)` — issues a request from Node and returns the response body.\\n- `await browserFetch(url, options)` — issues a request from the current browser page context and returns the response body.\\n- `help(name)` — prints usage for a given helper, e.g. `cliLog(help('click'))`.\\n\\n\\n### Task spaces\\n\\nA task space is an **isolated browsing context** that ego-browser provides for AI Agents. Each task space has its own set of tabs but **inherits the current user's login state** by default, so Agents can operate on authenticated sites without competing with or disturbing the user's normal browser windows.\\n\\nClosing all tabs in a task space is equivalent to closing that task space.\\n\\nA task often takes multiple heredoc rounds to complete. Because the Node.js runtime exits after each heredoc and retains no state, normal working heredocs should start with an explicit call to `useOrCreateTaskSpace(nameOrId)` to reuse the same space — this lets you operate continuously and reuse tabs across rounds. The exception is resuming after a handoff: once the user confirms \\\"continue\\\" (through an Ask or in chat), start the next heredoc with `takeOverTaskSpace(nameOrId)` instead.\\n\\n`nameOrId` can be a task space name, numeric id, or digit-only numeric id string. String values match `name`/`taskId` first, then digit-only strings fall back to numeric id. Number values match existing numeric ids only; if no matching id exists, `useOrCreateTaskSpace` fails instead of creating a new space.\\n\\nUse a short name for the active user goal when creating a new task space. Keep reusing that task space for follow-up questions, corrections, refinements, re-checks, and result validation, even if you previously thought the task was complete. Choose a new task space only when the user clearly starts a separate, unrelated goal. Prefer using the numeric `id` returned by `useOrCreateTaskSpace` (for example, `task.id`) to resume a known task in later rounds and avoid name collisions.\\n\\nFor any follow-up on the same user goal — including continue, corrections, retries, validation, user-reported problems, or work after `completeTaskSpace(..., { keep: true })` — resume the original task space first if it still exists. Do not create a new task space for the same goal unless the user asks for a fresh space, starts an unrelated goal, or the original space is unavailable after checking. If a new space is necessary, state why.\\n\\nAfter explicit user confirmation, to continue work from an existing user-owned, inactive, or unassigned task space, use `await listTaskSpaces()` to find the space, call `await claimTaskSpace(id)` to take ownership and select it, then use `await listTabs()` and `await switchTab(targetId)` to select the exact tab before acting.\\n\\n**Ownership policy** — every task space has `ownership: 'agent' | 'agentDelegatedToUser' | 'user'`; the helpers treat user-owned spaces differently:\\n\\n| Helper | When the target space is user-owned |\\n|---|---|\\n| `switchTaskSpace` | throws — agent-owned spaces only |\\n| `claimTaskSpace` | claims it (ownership transfers to the agent), then selects it |\\n| `handOffTaskSpace` | skipped — resolves `{ done: false, skipped: 'user-owned' }` |\\n| `completeTaskSpace(…, { keep: true })` | skipped — resolves `{ done: false, skipped: 'user-owned' }` |\\n| `completeTaskSpace(…, { keep: false })` | claims it, then closes it |\\n| `takeOverTaskSpace` / `waitForAgentControl` | no ownership check |\\n\\n`handOffTaskSpace` and `completeTaskSpace` resolve `{ done: true }` when the operation actually happened. Check `done` before telling the user the handoff/cleanup is finished — a `skipped` result usually means you targeted a space that was never yours.\\n\\n**`completeTaskSpace(nameOrId, { keep })` must occupy its own dedicated final heredoc, and run only after a prior heredoc's output has confirmed the task is genuinely done.** `keep` is required and defaults by policy to `false`: close the task space after completion unless there is a concrete reason to leave the live page visible.\\n\\nUse `{ keep: true }` only when the user explicitly asks to keep the page open, the task needs manual user action in that exact page, or the result cannot be delivered well as a URL, file, artifact, or summary. Do not keep a task space open merely because a page was visited, a document was created, or a screenshot was used for verification.\\n\\nWhen passing a string that may create a new task space, the string should reflect the task's intent (e.g. `'search github issues'`); don't use literal placeholders.\\n\\n**If the task space needs to be preserved after the task ends, keep only the tabs that need to be shown to the user.** Keep loose awareness of how many tabs are open — a quick `(await listTabs()).length` is enough; there's no need to spend a dedicated round just to check. When scratch tabs (search-result pages, cross-check pages, and other one-off pages) pile up, close them as you go rather than letting them all accumulate for the end. When finishing with `{ keep: true }` to leave pages for the user, clear out the remaining scratch tabs so only the pages worth showing stay open. Close a single tab with `await closeTab(targetId)` (`targetId` comes from `listTabs()` or an `openOrReuseTab` return value).\\n\\n\\n### Control handoff\\n\\nOnly one side — agent or user — holds control of a task space at any time. While the user holds control, any browser operation by the agent fails with a \\\"user is controlling\\\" message — do not retry it; follow the steps below to resume.\\n\\nA \\\"user is controlling\\\" error is a hard stop on the whole task — not an obstacle to route around. It means the user has deliberately taken the browser back, often because your current approach is going wrong. Honoring it *is* the correct outcome here; pushing the goal forward anyway is the failure. The only thing you may do is **ask the user and wait**.\\n\\nAn \\\"inactive\\\", \\\"not assigned to an agent\\\", or similar task-space error is also a hard stop with the same confirmation requirement. Resume only after explicit user confirmation, then start with `await claimTaskSpace(id)`.\\n\\n**Handing off**: When the task requires user intervention (e.g. login, captcha, manual confirmation), call `await handOffTaskSpace([nameOrId])` to give control to the user, and tell them exactly what to do. Omitting `nameOrId` uses the currently selected task space; pass `task.id` across heredoc rounds to avoid ambiguity.\\n\\n**Regaining control**: Take control back *only* after the user explicitly confirms — through an Ask (your harness's button/option prompt, e.g. \\\"Continue\\\" vs \\\"Finish task\\\") or a \\\"continue\\\" message in chat. Then start a new heredoc with `await takeOverTaskSpace([nameOrId])` and resume; if the user chooses to finish, close out with `await completeTaskSpace(nameOrId, { keep })`. Never call `takeOverTaskSpace` on your own to grab control back — it has no ownership check and will seize the browser away from the user.\\n\\n**Unexpected takeover**: The user can take over at any time via the browser GUI — the same effect as the agent calling `handOffTaskSpace`. Do not retry the failed operation and do not auto-takeover; surface the Ask above (Continue / Finish) and resume only when the user picks Continue.\\n\\n`await waitForAgentControl(nameOrId)` is a read-only blocking poll (it never takes control); use it only to wait inside the current heredoc for a handoff you initiated.\\n\\n\\n### Scroll / mouse\\n\\n```js\\n// DOM scroll\\nawait scrollBy(900)\\nawait scrollToBottomUntil(\\n  async () => await js(String.raw`document.querySelectorAll('article').length`) >= 20,\\n  { step: 900, wait: 1, maxSteps: 20 }\\n)\\n\\n// Real wheel event\\nawait scroll({ dy: 900 })\\n```\\n\\nElement-target helpers such as `click`, `doubleClick`, `hover`, `dragMouse`, `fillInput`, `uploadFile`, and `waitForElement` accept the same selector/ref surface: raw CSS, `xpath=...`, `@N` / `ref=N`, and `loc=...` values from `snapshotText()` (`loc=css:...`, `loc=role:...`, `loc=href:...`). `@N` refs are for ego-browser helpers only; they are not valid selectors inside `document.querySelector(...)`.\\n\\n`click`, `doubleClick`, `hover`, and `dragMouse` share these target formats. Coordinates are in CSS pixels:\\n\\n- `string` — CSS selector, `xpath=...`, `@N` / `ref=N`, or `loc=...`; clicks the element's center.\\n- `[x, y]` or `{x, y}` — viewport coordinates.\\n- `{selector}` — CSS selector, `xpath=...`, `@N` / `ref=N`, or `loc=...`; clicks the element's center.\\n- `{selector, x, y}` — offset from the element's top-left corner by `x`/`y`.\\n- `options.label` (optional) — a 3-6 word action description; triggers a visual highlight animation.\\n\\n```js\\nawait click('@21', { label: 'check login status' })\\nawait click('button.primary', { label: 'click submit button' })\\nawait click([420, 260])\\nawait click({ x: 420, y: 260 })\\nawait click({ selector: 'canvas#stage', x: 12, y: 8 })\\nawait hover('@5', { label: 'hover to reveal menu' })\\nawait dragMouse([from, to], { label: 'drag card' })\\n```\\n\\n### uploadFile\\n\\n```js\\nawait uploadFile('input[type=\\\"file\\\"]', \\\"/absolute/path/to/file.pdf\\\")\\n```\\n\\n### js\\n\\n`js()` is essentially `Runtime.evaluate` and takes a string. You can pass a function, but doing so triggers a one-time warning and wraps it via `.toString()` — closures are not captured and there is no argument channel. **维度覆盖**：矩阵包含 21 列（1 列粘性首列“设计领域 / 设计要素” + 20 个关键确证试验）及 27 个设计要素行，涵盖研究身份、分期与状态、国家地区、随机盲法、试验组/对照组干预、给药方案、主要终点定义与时间点、访视随访、样本量、分析人群、统计模型、多重性控制等。\n- **粘性首列**：第一列在横向滚动时保持粘性冻结，便于医学经理横向对照不同药物方案。\n\n#### (3) 矩阵单元格下钻与原文定位实测\n- **触发操作**：在矩阵中点击 NCT02260986（CHRONOS）的试验标识单元格按钮（`BUTTON.kz-c-matrix-cell-trigger`）。\n- **抽屉呈现**：数据依据抽屉弹出，显示证据标识 `c-nct02260986-trial_identity`、来源版本 `ClinicalTrials.gov`、定位章节 `Identification` 及英文原始摘录片段，实现了从概览要素到原始披露文本的单跳穿透。\n\n---\n\n### 5. 发现项清单（Defect & Optimization Log）\n\n| 编号 | 严重级别 | 涉及报告 / 页面 | 复现操作 | 观察到的实际现象 | 对医学经理的临床工作影响 | 最小修复建议 |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **OBS-01** | **重要缺陷** | Report C (`design-map.html`) | 在 1024px/1280px 视口下向下滚动矩阵至第 15~27 行 | 表头包含 NCT 号、药品中文名、英文名、分期、国家列表等丰富信息，在窄视口下换行导致表头高度达 140~180px；向下滚动时吸顶表头挤占了约 20%~25% 纵向视口 | 限制了下方设计要素内容区的可视行数，医学经理需频繁上下滚动比对 | 在页面向下滚动离开初始表头区后，吸顶表头自动切为“精简模式”（仅保留药名+NCT号单行胶囊，高度降至 40px），鼠标悬浮或点击可展开完整卡片 |\n| **OBS-02** | **重要缺陷** | Report B (`efficacy.html`) | 浏览跨试验疗效横向比较柱状图（如 FACIT 疲劳变化） | 柱状图将 Study 301（第26周）与 APPLY-PNH（第24周）等并列展示，顶部虽有“约6个月”说明，但 X 轴标签仅显示 `产品名｜试验名` | 临床试验时间点存在 2 周至数周差异，若 X 轴未直接显式携带时间点，快节奏汇报或跨部门讨论时易忽略时间窗微小差异 | 在柱状图 X 轴试验名后或图例中，增加时间点胶囊标签（如 `CHAMPION-301 [W26]`、`APPLY-PNH [W24]`） |\n| **OBS-03** | **一般优化** | Report A (`overview.html`) | 点击产品条目打开抽屉，切换至“安全性”或“数据依据”页签，复制浏览器地址栏 URL 在新标签打开 | 抽屉打开时 URL 更新了产品 hash（如 `#dupilumab`），但未携带激活的页签状态（`tab=safety`），重新打开默认落回疗效页签 | 医学经理无法将特定安全性数据或来源依据视图直接作为链接分享给药物安全或注册同事 | 在页签切换时，同步更新 URL Hash（如 `#dupilumab?tab=safety`），并在初次载入时根据 URL 自动定位到指定页签 |\n| **OBS-04** | **一般优化** | Report B (`disposition-overview.html`) | 查看受试者完成情况数据表格中的“单位”列 | “筛选失败”、“完成研究”等计数的“单位”列显示为 `未列示`（例数写在指标名称中） | 中文医学报告中，计数的单位通常直观使用“例”或“人”，“未列示”易被误读为数据缺失 | 当指标为计数时，单位列回填为“例”或保留连贯的临床计数描述 |\n| **OBS-05** | **一般优化** | Report C (`inclusion-criteria.html` / `exclusion-criteria.html`) | 查看详细入选/排除标准表格 | 部分较长标准文本在单元格内折叠截断 | 医学经理难以一眼判断该标准是否完整显示 | 在截断文本末尾增加明显的 `[展开全文]` 或悬浮 Tooltip 提示 |\n\n---\n\n## Evidence And
